card.name: Bedara Vesha
card.era: Legend of roughly 300 years (post-Vijayanagara Sonda era)
card.profile: Bedara Vesha ('Hunter Dance') is a folk dance performed on the nights before Holi in Sirsi town, Uttara Kannada, Karnataka, staged every alternate year and drawing large crowds across five days (Wikipedia). It is tied to a roughly 300-year-old legend from the Sonda dynasty era about the warrior Malleshi of the Beda community. Around 50 solo artists perform in elaborate costume - including a giant bundle of peacock feathers restrained by ropes - accompanied by whistle-blowers and tamate (hand-drum) beaters, performing through the night and culminating at the Shri Marikamba Temple (Satyaagrah; MetroSaga).
card.insight: Dollu Kunitha is also performed during the Bedara Vesha festivities, and one performer is traditionally barred from looking another in the face, underscoring the ritual discipline behind the spectacle (Satyaagrah).
